jurisdiction.name: United Nations
jurisdiction.overview: Official documents of this organisation are listed on its own page and are not counted in member countries' totals.

narrative.summary: The UN General Assembly has adopted a series of resolutions on AI since 2023, including resolution 78/265 on safe, secure and trustworthy AI, resolution 78/311 on AI capacity-building, the Global Digital Compact (2024), and resolution 79/325 establishing an Independent International Scientific Panel on AI and a Global Dialogue on AI Governance. Separate resolutions address AI in the military domain, lethal autonomous weapons and AI in nuclear command and control. The Human Rights Council has adopted resolutions on digital technologies and on privacy that set human rights expectations for AI.
lead_institutions: United Nations System Chief Executives Board for Coordination
Office for Digital and Emerging Technologies

instruments.official_title: Seizing the opportunities of safe, secure and trustworthy artificial intelligence systems for sustainable development (A/RES/78/265)
instruments.english_title: Seizing the opportunities of safe, secure and trustworthy artificial intelligence systems for sustainable development
instruments.summary: General Assembly resolution encouraging Member States and other stakeholders to promote safe, secure and trustworthy AI systems that respect human rights and support the Sustainable Development Goals, to develop regulatory and governance approaches and safeguards, to close digital divides between and within countries, and to cooperate on capacity-building for developing countries.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the General Assembly without a vote on 21 March 2024 (A/RES/78/265).
instruments.evidence_reference: Adoption date read on the official UN DGACM resolutions report (public.e-delegate.un.org/reports/ga78_resolutions.html), read 2026-10-21. docs.un.org viewer is script-rendered; summary from known text, consistent with title and later resolutions citing it (e.g. ITU WTSA Res. 101). | Independent check 2026-10-21: docs.un.org is JS-only; UN Digital Library record 4043244 confirms title, A/RES/78/265, 21 March 2024, adopted without a vote at the 63rd plenary meeting.; 'A non-binding resolution' and 'the first General Assembly resolution dedicated to AI' are not stated in the source.

instruments.official_title: Enhancing international cooperation on capacity-building of artificial intelligence (A/RES/78/311)
instruments.english_title: Enhancing international cooperation on capacity-building of artificial intelligence
instruments.summary: Resolves to bridge AI and other digital divides between and within countries and to strengthen international cooperation on AI capacity-building for developing countries through North-South, South-South and triangular cooperation. Invites Member States and the UN system to include AI capacity-building in national plans and requests a report from the Secretary-General.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the General Assembly on 1 July 2024 at its 97th plenary meeting (A/RES/78/311). A non-binding resolution.
instruments.evidence_reference: Adoption date read on the official UN DGACM resolutions report (public.e-delegate.un.org/reports/ga78_resolutions.html), read 2026-10-21. Date also printed on the English PDF (opened). | Independent check 2026-10-21: corrected from the official source.

instruments.official_title: Global Digital Compact (annex I to resolution 79/1, The Pact for the Future)
instruments.english_title: Global Digital Compact
instruments.summary: A global framework for digital cooperation and the governance of artificial intelligence, annexed to the Pact for the Future. Its AI commitments include establishing an Independent International Scientific Panel on AI and a Global Dialogue on AI Governance within the UN, strengthening AI capacity-building partnerships, considering options for innovative financing of AI capacity, and supporting interoperable data governance frameworks.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the General Assembly without a vote on 22 September 2024 as part of resolution 79/1 (The Pact for the Future); opened for endorsement in September 2024.
instruments.evidence_reference: Adoption date and 'adopted without vote, 3rd plenary meeting' from UN Digital Library record 4061879 (A/RES/79/1), which lists the Global Digital Compact as contained in the resolution. AI commitments from the UN GDC page. | Independent check 2026-10-21: UN Digital Library record 4061879 confirms A/RES/79/1 (The Pact for the Future) adopted without a vote on 22 Sept 2024 and containing the Global Digital Compact; GDC page confirms it was opened for endorsement in September 2024 and lists the AI commitments.; Neither source calls it 'non-binding'. The official_pdf_url is the draft A/79/L.2, not the adopted text.

instruments.official_title: Terms of reference and modalities for the establishment and functioning of the Independent International Scientific Panel on Artificial Intelligence and the Global Dialogue on Artificial Intelligence Governance (A/RES/79/325)
instruments.english_title: Terms of reference and modalities for the establishment and functioning of the Independent International Scientific Panel on Artificial Intelligence and the Global Dialogue on Artificial Intelligence Governance
instruments.summary: Establishes a 40-member Independent International Scientific Panel on AI, serving three-year terms in a personal capacity, to issue an annual policy-relevant but non-prescriptive scientific summary on AI opportunities, risks and impacts. Also establishes an annual Global Dialogue on AI Governance among governments and stakeholders, held alternately in Geneva and New York, starting in Geneva in 2026 alongside the AI for Good summit.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the General Assembly on 26 August 2025 at its 89th plenary meeting (A/RES/79/325).
instruments.evidence_reference: Adoption date read on the official UN DGACM resolutions report (public.e-delegate.un.org/reports/ga79_resolutions.html), read 2026-10-21. Date and content confirmed on the official PDF (documents.un.org) and on the PGA-hosted copy. Panel appointment from UN press release GA/12751 (meeting date not printed there). | Independent check 2026-10-21: A/RES/79/325 (PDF on un.org/pga) confirms title, adoption 26 Aug 2025 at the 89th plenary meeting, 40 members in personal capacity for three-year terms, annual policy-relevant but non-prescriptive summary report, Dialogue alternating Geneva/New York starting Geneva 2026 alongside AI for Good.; 'Without a vote' is not printed in the text checked; appointment of members in 2026 and term dates 12 Feb 2026-11 Feb 2029 are not in the source. official_pdf_url on documents.un.org could not be fetched (robots).

instruments.official_title: Artificial intelligence in the military domain and its implications for international peace and security (A/RES/79/239)
instruments.english_title: Artificial intelligence in the military domain and its implications for international peace and security
instruments.summary: General Assembly resolution on AI in the military domain. It affirms that international law applies throughout all stages of the life cycle of AI in the military domain, and requests the Secretary-General to seek the views of States, with specific focus on areas other than lethal autonomous weapons systems, and of other stakeholders, and to report to the General Assembly at its eightieth session.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the General Assembly by recorded vote (159-2-5) on 24 December 2024 (A/RES/79/239).
instruments.evidence_reference: Adoption date read on the official UN DGACM resolutions report (public.e-delegate.un.org/reports/ga79_resolutions.html), read 2026-10-21. UNODA page (disarmament.unoda.org/en/node/87368) confirms date and the follow-up SG report A/80/78. | Independent check 2026-10-21: UN Digital Library record 4071348 confirms title, 24 Dec 2024, recorded vote 159-2-5 at the 55th plenary; text confirms OP1 on international law across the AI life cycle and OP7 request to the SG with focus on areas other than LAWS.; 'Non-binding' and 'the General Assembly's first resolution on AI in the military domain' are not stated in the source.

instruments.official_title: Artificial intelligence in the military domain and its implications for international peace and security (A/RES/80/58)
instruments.english_title: Artificial intelligence in the military domain and its implications for international peace and security
instruments.summary: Follow-up resolution on AI in the military domain. It decides to convene a three-day meeting in Geneva in 2026 for States to exchange perspectives on the Secretary-General's report, open also to international and regional organisations, the ICRC, academia, civil society and industry, with a factual summary to the First Committee at its eighty-first session.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the General Assembly on 5 December 2025 (A/RES/80/58).
instruments.evidence_reference: Conflicting dates: UN press release GA/12736 shows 80/58 (L.46), 80/57 and 80/23 adopted at the same 52nd plenary meeting, and 80/57 and 80/23 print 1 December 2025; a UNODA note verbale (unodaweb-meetings.unoda.org/public/2026-04/NV AIMD informal exchanges States.pdf) says 'adopted by the General Assembly on 5 December 2025'. Recorded month only. Full text not opened; summary limited to what UNODA documents state (informal exchanges 2026). Vote from GA/12736. | Independent check 2026-10-21: docs.un.org is JS-only; no UN Digital Library record found in one search. UNODA note verbale (official) confirms the title and adoption on 5 December 2025, and that the Assembly decided to convene a three-day meeting in Geneva in 2026 (held 15-17 June 2026) open to States, international and regional organisations, the ICRC, academia, civil society and industry.; Recorded vote 167-5-5, draft A/C.1/80/L.46 and 'non-binding' could not be confirmed from an official source.

instruments.official_title: Possible risks of the integration of artificial intelligence into command, control and communications systems of nuclear weapons (A/RES/80/23)
instruments.english_title: Possible risks of the integration of artificial intelligence into command, control and communications systems of nuclear weapons
instruments.summary: Demands that, pending the total elimination of nuclear weapons, human control and oversight be maintained over nuclear command, control and communications systems, including those integrating AI. Urges nuclear-weapon States to adopt and publish policies keeping AI-enabled systems under human control and ensuring they do not autonomously initiate decisions on nuclear use, and calls for common understandings and confidence-building measures.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the General Assembly on 1 December 2025 at its 52nd plenary meeting, on the report of the First Committee (A/80/534).
instruments.evidence_reference: Date printed on the English PDF (UN Digital Library record 4095461). Vote from UN press release GA/12736. | Independent check 2026-10-21: UN Digital Library PDF confirms title, adoption 1 Dec 2025 at the 52nd plenary meeting on the First Committee report (A/80/534) and the operative content.; Recorded vote 118-9-44 is not printed in the document or on the record page as fetched; 'non-binding' not stated.

instruments.official_title: Lethal autonomous weapons systems (A/RES/78/241)
instruments.english_title: Lethal autonomous weapons systems
instruments.summary: General Assembly resolution stressing the urgent need for the international community to address the challenges raised by autonomous weapons systems, including from humanitarian, legal, security, technological and ethical perspectives, and requesting the Secretary-General to seek the views of States and other stakeholders and to report to the General Assembly.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the General Assembly by recorded vote (152-4-11) on 22 December 2023 (A/RES/78/241).
instruments.evidence_reference: Adoption date read on the official UN DGACM resolutions report (public.e-delegate.un.org/reports/ga78_resolutions.html), read 2026-10-21. Text not opened; summary from known content of the resolution and the follow-up 79/62 which notes the SG report it requested. | Independent check 2026-10-21: UN Digital Library record 4033027 confirms A/RES/78/241, 22 Dec 2023, vote 152-4-11 at the 50th plenary.; 'Non-binding' and 'the General Assembly's first resolution on lethal autonomous weapons systems' not stated in the source; resolution PDF could not be fetched.

instruments.official_title: Lethal autonomous weapons systems (A/RES/79/62)
instruments.english_title: Lethal autonomous weapons systems
instruments.summary: Takes note of the Secretary-General's report on lethal autonomous weapons systems, urges the Group of Governmental Experts under the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons to complete its mandate, ideally by the end of 2025, and decides to hold two days of open informal consultations in New York in 2025 for all States and stakeholders to complement that work.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the General Assembly by recorded vote (166-3-15) on 2 December 2024 (A/RES/79/62).
instruments.evidence_reference: Date printed on the official PDF (documents.un.org). | Independent check 2026-10-21: UN Digital Library record 4071100 confirms A/RES/79/62, 2 Dec 2024, vote 166-3-15 at the 44th plenary; PDF confirms summary (SG report, GGE preferably by end of 2025, two days of informal consultations in New York in 2025).; 'Non-binding' not stated. official_pdf_url on documents.un.org could not be fetched (robots).

instruments.official_title: Lethal autonomous weapons systems (A/RES/80/57)
instruments.english_title: Lethal autonomous weapons systems
instruments.summary: Stresses the need for an inclusive multilateral approach to the legal, technological, ethical, humanitarian and security concerns raised by lethal autonomous weapons systems. Calls for action within the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons and asks its High Contracting Parties to complete, through the Group of Governmental Experts, a set of elements with a view to future negotiations.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the General Assembly by recorded vote (164-6-7) on 1 December 2025 (A/RES/80/57).
instruments.evidence_reference: Date printed on the English PDF. Vote from UN press release GA/12736. | Independent check 2026-10-21: UN Digital Library record 4095989 and PDF confirm A/RES/80/57, 1 Dec 2025, vote 164-6-7 at the 52nd plenary, and summary content.; 'Non-binding' not stated.

instruments.official_title: Promotion and protection of human rights in the context of digital technologies (A/RES/78/213)
instruments.english_title: Promotion and protection of human rights in the context of digital technologies
instruments.summary: Resolution on human rights in the digital context with dedicated paragraphs on AI. It affirms that human rights must be respected throughout the life cycle of AI systems and calls on States and other stakeholders to carry out human rights impact assessments, to refrain from or cease AI uses that cannot operate in line with international human rights law or pose undue risks, to promote transparency and explainability, and to ensure participation of all relevant stakeholders in AI decisions.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the General Assembly on 19 December 2023 at its 50th plenary meeting (A/RES/78/213).
instruments.evidence_reference: Adoption date read on the official UN DGACM resolutions report (public.e-delegate.un.org/reports/ga78_resolutions.html), read 2026-10-21. Text opened: AI in operative paras 19-21. | Independent check 2026-10-21: UN Digital Library PDF confirms title, A/RES/78/213, adoption 19 Dec 2023 at the 50th plenary meeting and AI paragraphs 19-21.; 'Without a vote' is not printed in the text and the record page did not show vote data; 'non-binding' not stated.; Para 21 refers to participation of 'all relevant stakeholders', not specifically affected people.

instruments.official_title: The right to privacy in the digital age (A/RES/77/211)
instruments.english_title: The right to privacy in the digital age
instruments.summary: Resolution on privacy in the digital age with dedicated provisions on AI. It calls on States and companies to address the privacy and human rights risks of AI through regulation, transparency, audits, redress and human oversight, to conduct human rights due diligence across the AI life cycle, and calls on businesses to respect privacy when designing and deploying AI and to address discrimination and harm from automated decision-making.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the General Assembly without a vote on 15 December 2022 at its 54th plenary meeting (A/RES/77/211).
instruments.evidence_reference: Date printed on the English PDF (opened). AI in operative paras 6, 7(h), 8(d), 8(g), 10. Earlier GA privacy resolutions (75/176, 73/179) not checked for AI content. | Independent check 2026-10-21: UN Digital Library record 3999709 confirms A/RES/77/211, 15 Dec 2022, adopted without a vote at the 54th plenary.; 'Non-binding' not stated.

instruments.official_title: The right to privacy in the digital age (A/RES/79/175)
instruments.english_title: The right to privacy in the digital age
instruments.summary: Resolution on privacy in the digital age with dedicated provisions on AI. It calls for human rights due diligence and impact assessments throughout the life cycle of AI systems, rights-based auditing, redress and human oversight; raises concerns about remote biometric surveillance and facial recognition without safeguards; and urges States to refrain from or cease using AI applications that cannot operate in line with human rights law.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the General Assembly without a vote on 17 December 2024 at its 53rd plenary meeting (A/RES/79/175).
instruments.evidence_reference: Adoption date read on the official UN DGACM resolutions report (public.e-delegate.un.org/reports/ga79_resolutions.html), read 2026-10-21. Date also printed on the official PDF (opened). | Independent check 2026-10-21: UN Digital Library record 4071978 confirms A/RES/79/175, 17 Dec 2024, adopted without a vote at the 53rd plenary. Resolution text could not be fetched (documents.un.org blocked; DL file errored) so summary not checked line by line.; 'Non-binding' not stated.

instruments.official_title: The right to privacy in the digital age (A/HRC/RES/42/15)
instruments.english_title: The right to privacy in the digital age
instruments.summary: Recognises that AI can affect the right to privacy and other rights and calls for risks to be addressed through regulation, human-centred auditing and redress. Calls on States to review rules on profiling, automated decision-making and machine learning, and to consider requiring businesses to integrate human rights into AI design and deployment. Requests an expert seminar and a report from the High Commissioner on AI and privacy.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Human Rights Council without a vote on 26 September 2019 at its 39th meeting (A/HRC/RES/42/15).
instruments.evidence_reference: Date printed on the official PDF (document dated 7 October 2019; adoption 26 September 2019, 39th meeting). | Independent check 2026-10-21: UN Digital Library record 3837297 confirms A/HRC/RES/42/15 adopted without a vote on 26 Sept 2019 at the 39th meeting. instruments.english_title: Right to privacy in the digital age
instruments.summary: Human Rights Council resolution on privacy in the digital age that addresses AI, profiling and automated decision-making as part of its call on States and businesses to protect the right to privacy.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Human Rights Council without a vote on 7 October 2021 at its 41st meeting (A/HRC/RES/48/4).

instruments.official_title: New and emerging digital technologies and human rights (A/HRC/RES/53/29)
instruments.english_title: New and emerging digital technologies and human rights
instruments.summary: Human Rights Council resolution with provisions on AI. It calls for human rights to be respected throughout the life cycle of AI systems, including by preventing harm and discrimination and ensuring transparency, explainability and lawful data handling; urges stronger oversight and enforcement capacity for AI; and requests a mapping report on human rights work on AI, OHCHR advisory capacity on AI, and an expert consultation on business and human rights in AI.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Human Rights Council without a vote on 14 July 2023 at its 37th meeting (A/HRC/RES/53/29).
instruments.evidence_reference: Date printed on the official PDF (opened). | Independent check 2026-10-21: UN Digital Library record 4020206 confirms A/HRC/RES/53/29 adopted without a vote on 14 July 2023 at the 37th meeting. Text not fetched.; 'Non-binding' not stated; 'the Human Rights Council's most detailed provisions on AI to date' is an unsupported evaluative claim.

instruments.official_title: Right to privacy in the digital age (A/HRC/RES/54/21)
instruments.english_title: Right to privacy in the digital age
instruments.summary: Calls on States and businesses to minimise the risks of AI and other emerging technologies through human rights due diligence, impact assessments across the system life cycle, human oversight and redress, and to combat AI-driven discrimination. Notes that some AI applications, such as automated decision-making and profiling, may not comply with human rights law without safeguards, and urges transparency, explainability, representative training data and limits on facial recognition and biometric surveillance.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Human Rights Council without a vote on 12 October 2023 at its 48th meeting (A/HRC/RES/54/21).
instruments.evidence_reference: Date printed on the official PDF (opened). | Independent check 2026-10-21: UN Digital Library record 4025243 confirms A/HRC/RES/54/21 adopted without a vote on 12 Oct 2023 at the 48th meeting. Text not fetched.; 'Non-binding' not stated.

instruments.english_title: New and emerging digital technologies and human rights

instruments.official_title: UNCITRAL Model Law on Automated Contracting (2024)
instruments.english_title: UNCITRAL Model Law on Automated Contracting
instruments.issuing_authority: United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL)
instruments.publisher_name: United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL)
instruments.summary: Model legislation that States may enact to give legal recognition to the use of automation, including AI techniques, smart contracts and machine-to-machine transactions, in forming and performing contracts. Published with a Guide to Enactment.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by UNCITRAL on 11 July 2024 as internationally acceptable rules for national legislators; accompanied by a Guide to Enactment.
instruments.evidence_reference: Date and AI relevance from the UNCITRAL page. The page lists GA resolution 79/119 'Model Law on Automated Contracting' (adopted 4 Dec 2024 per e-delegate report) but the page does not state the relationship; not stated in current_status. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title, 11 July 2024 adoption and description confirmed on uncitral.un.org.; Page does not state the model law is 'not binding in itself'; it describes rules for national legislators.

instruments.official_title: Principles for the Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence in the United Nations System
instruments.english_title: Principles for the Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence in the United Nations System
instruments.issuing_authority: United Nations System Chief Executives Board for Coordination (CEB)
instruments.publisher_name: United Nations System Chief Executives Board for Coordination (CEB)
instruments.summary: Ten principles, grounded in ethics and human rights and based on the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI, to guide the use of AI across all stages of the life cycle by UN system entities: do no harm; defined purpose, necessity and proportionality; safety and security; fairness and non-discrimination; sustainability; privacy and data governance; human autonomy and oversight; transparency and explainability; responsibility and accountability; inclusion and participation.
instruments.current_status: Endorsed by the UN System Chief Executives Board for Coordination in September 2022, after approval by the High-level Committee on Programmes in July 2022; applies to the use of AI by UN system entities.
instruments.evidence_reference: Date and endorsement from CEB page (HLCP approved July 2022; CEB endorsed September 2022). CEB members are UN system organisations, not States. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title, CEB endorsement September 2022, HLCP development, ten principles and UNESCO basis confirmed.; 'Not addressed to Member States' is not stated on the page.
